name: Bahrain
summary: No free movement for anyone; EU, US and other passports use the same Golden Residency categories (Resolution 20 of 2022): property (BHD 130,000 since the NPRA announcement of 26 November 2025, still BHD 200,000 on the portal page), employees with 5 years' residence and BHD 2,000 salary, retirees, and talented individuals. No remote-work visa was found. Citizenship is not realistically open.
naturalisation: Not researched from the Bahraini Nationality Law in this pass. Golden Residency does not lead to citizenship.
dual_citizenship_note: General rule, not verified in this pass: Bahrain does not generally allow dual nationality for naturalised citizens.

routes.name: Golden Residency - property owners
routes.summary: Own Bahraini property worth at least BHD 130,000 and get a 10-year renewable residence without a sponsor.
routes.requirements: NPRA announced on 26 November 2025 a cut of the minimum from BHD 200,000 to BHD 130,000. The Bahrain National Portal page (undated) still says title deed value of at least BHD 200,000. Documents: valid health insurance in Bahrain, passport valid 6+ months, title deed, 6-month bank statement. Processing 5 working days.
routes.fees_note: BHD 5 application (non-refundable) plus BHD 300 for the 10-year permit.
routes.physical_presence: Not stated on the portal; one source reports 90 days a year (unconfirmed).
routes.family: Spouse, children and parents can be included (secondary source).
routes.tax_note: Bahrain has no personal income tax.

routes.name: Golden Residency - employees living in Bahrain
routes.summary: Residents with 5 years in Bahrain and a salary of at least BHD 2,000 a month can switch to a 10-year Golden Residency.
routes.requirements: NPRA: 5 years of residence in Bahrain and average basic salary of at least BHD 2,000 over the last 5 years (portal wording; salary certificate shows minimum BHD 2,000). Documents: health insurance, 6-month bank statement. Processing 5 working days.
routes.fees_note: BHD 5 plus BHD 300 every 10 years. Income is BHD 2,000 a month x 12; the period is monthly per secondary sources, not stated on the NPRA page.
routes.tax_note: Bahrain has no personal income tax.

routes.name: Golden Residency - retirees
routes.summary: Retirees with a pension of BHD 2,000 a month (resident) or BHD 4,000 a month (living abroad) can get Golden Residency.
routes.requirements: Resident retirees: 15 years of work in Bahrain and a pension above BHD 2,000 a month (Gulf News). Non-resident retirees: pension above BHD 4,000 a month. Official criteria text not read; the NPRA page covers employees and retirees under one service.
routes.fees_note: BHD 5 plus BHD 300. Income shown is the non-resident figure, BHD 4,000 x 12; resident retirees BHD 24,000.
routes.tax_note: Bahrain has no personal income tax.

routes.name: Golden Residency - highly talented individuals
routes.summary: A 10-year residency for people with a recognised talent certificate in academic, sporting, entrepreneurial, artistic or literary fields.
routes.requirements: Talent certificate required; no numeric criteria on the portal. Processing 10 working days.
routes.tax_note: Bahrain has no personal income tax.

routes.name: Employer-sponsored work residence
routes.summary: Most expatriates live in Bahrain on a work permit and residence permit through an employer (LMRA/NPRA); companies can be 100% foreign owned in most sectors.
routes.requirements: Employer applies for a work visa via LMRA and NPRA; residence tied to the job. Not researched in detail.
routes.tax_note: Bahrain has no personal income tax.

open_questions: Property threshold conflict: the Bahrain National Portal page (undated) still says BHD 200,000; NPRA announced BHD 130,000 on 26 November 2025. The effective date is not stated.
Retiree and salary criteria differ across secondary sources (one 2026 report says BHD 4,000 salary for professionals); the NPRA wording was only partly readable.
Annual minimum stay (90 days reported) is unconfirmed.
Bahrain remote-work or digital nomad visa: none found.
Naturalisation years and dual-nationality rule not researched.
